chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 81 — The Heavenly Tablets and Enoch's Commission
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No securely corresponding wording from Chapter 81 has been identified in the surviving Aramaic manuscripts of the Astronomical Book, and no extant Greek witness preserves it. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is therefore the translation base for all ten verses: the heavenly tablets, the record of human deeds, Enoch's blessing, his return to earth and his commission to teach Methuselah and his children. The reading of three holy ones in verse 5 and the difficult statement about the righteous in verse 9 are translated as preserved in this Geʽez text rather than replaced by readings from later translations. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: He said to me, “Enoch, look at the book of the tablets of heaven. Read what is written upon them and understand each single thing.”
verses.study: Enoch is commanded to look, read and understand. Revelation requires attentive reception rather than passive wonder.
crossReferences: Habakkuk 2:2 — a vision is written so it can be read
Revelation 5:1–5 — a heavenly book contains sealed purposes

verses.text: I looked at all the tablets of heaven and read everything written there. I understood it all and read the book and everything written in it: all the deeds of humanity and of all the children of flesh who will be upon the earth throughout the generations of the world.
verses.study: The tablets hold a comprehensive record extending through human generations. Deeds are neither forgotten nor hidden from heavenly knowledge.
crossReferences: Psalm 139:16 — days are written in God's book
Daniel 7:10 — books are opened before the heavenly court

verses.text: Immediately I blessed the Lord, the King of Glory forever, because he made all the works of the world. I praised the Lord for his patience and for his blessing upon the children of the world.
verses.study: Knowledge of the record leads Enoch to worship. Creation, patience and blessing are praised together before judgment is discussed.
crossReferences: Psalm 24:7–10 — the Lord is acclaimed as the King of Glory
Romans 2:4 — divine patience is meant to lead people toward repentance

verses.text: Then I said, “Blessed is the person who dies righteous and good, against whom no book of violence has been written and in whom no error has been found.”
verses.study: Blessed death is linked to righteous goodness and the absence of recorded violence. The heavenly record gives moral weight to daily conduct.
crossReferences: Psalm 37:37 — the blameless and upright have a future of peace
Revelation 14:13 — those who die in the Lord are called blessed

verses.text: The three holy ones brought me near and set me upon the earth before the door of my house. They said to me, “Make everything known to your son Methuselah, and show all your children that no flesh is righteous before the Lord, for he is their Creator.”
verses.study: Return to the household becomes a teaching mission. Human dependence is grounded in the Lord's identity as Creator.
crossReferences: Job 4:17 — no mortal is more righteous than the Maker
Psalm 143:2 — no living person is righteous before God

verses.text: For one year we will leave you with your children until you regain strength, so that you may teach your children, write these things for them and testify to all your children. In the second year they will take you from among them.
verses.study: Enoch receives limited time for teaching, writing and testimony. The commission gives urgency to careful preservation for his family.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 6:6–7 — God's words are taught diligently to children
2 Peter 1:13–15 — teaching is preserved before the teacher's departure

verses.text: Let your heart be strong, for the good will make righteousness known to the good. The righteous will rejoice with the righteous and greet one another with joy.
verses.study: Strength is directed toward transmitting righteousness. Shared goodness creates recognition, fellowship and joy.
crossReferences: Psalm 97:11–12 — light and gladness are sown for the righteous
Malachi 3:16 — those who fear the Lord speak with one another

verses.text: The sinner will die with the sinner, and the one who turns aside will sink with the one who turns aside.
verses.study: Companionship in rebellion ends in shared ruin. The concise parallel warns that chosen paths form a common destiny.
crossReferences: Psalm 1:6 — the way of the wicked perishes
Matthew 15:14 — when the blind lead the blind, both fall

verses.text: Those who practice righteousness will die because of the deeds of humanity and will be gathered away because of the deeds of the wicked.
verses.study: The righteous may suffer and be removed because of others' evil deeds. Their death is not presented as proof that their righteousness failed.
crossReferences: Isaiah 57:1–2 — the righteous are taken away from coming evil
Wisdom 4:10–14 — the righteous are removed from surrounding wickedness

verses.text: In those days they finished speaking with me, and I went to my people while blessing the Lord of the worlds.
verses.study: The heavenly encounter ends with return, blessing and responsibility among Enoch's people. Revelation moves back into community life.
crossReferences: Luke 2:20 — witnesses return glorifying and praising God
Acts 1:8–12 — heavenly instruction is followed by earthly witness

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 81 moves from heavenly tablets to earthly responsibility. Enoch reads the record of human deeds across generations, then responds by blessing the King of Glory.
The tablets establish that violence and error are known. Yet Enoch first praises divine creation, patience and blessing, keeping judgment within the character of the Creator.
Three holy ones return Enoch to his home and command him to teach Methuselah and all his children. His remaining year becomes a period for instruction, writing and testimony.

The closing sayings distinguish righteous fellowship from shared rebellion and acknowledge that the righteous can be gathered away because of human wickedness. Enoch returns to his people blessing the Lord of the worlds.

crossReferences: Psalm 139:16 — human days are written in God's book
Daniel 7:10 — heavenly books are opened
Malachi 3:16 — a book of remembrance is written
Isaiah 57:1–2 — the righteous may be taken from evil
Revelation 14:13 — blessed are those who die in the Lord
2 Peter 1:12–15 — truth is preserved before a teacher's departure
